title: Nasal Tramazoline and Dexamethazone in Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) Patients Tramazoline and

sections.abstract: Nasal resistance presents considerable variations during night\[8\]. Additionally, Oral and oro-nasal breathing epochs exhibit strong correlation with the number of apnoea/hypopnoeas \[7\].The hypothesis that the present study aims to test is whether the pharmacological prevention of increased nasal resistance during night could alter breathing route pattern and lead to a decrease in the number of apnoea/hypopnoeas in OSA patients with normal nasal resistance.
